startHere: CSE ENGINEERING MASTER ROADMAP | SEM 3 → SEM 8
A comfortable, depth-first learning guide. The sequence is made of learning sessions, not calendar deadlines.
Purpose
Build broad, practical CSE engineering ability across Sem 3–8. Java is the starting language, not the final identity.
Your current starting point
Java revision completed through methods/functions. Start with Git/GitHub setup, then methods/arrays/strings consolidation.
Phase 1
Internship Preparation: Java, OOP, collections, DSA foundations, SQL, JDBC, Spring Boot, testing, security basics, deployment, basic React and interview evidence.
Phase 2

CSE Engineering Mastery: advanced DSA, JVM/concurrency, C, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, OS, networks, advanced DBMS, software design, security, system design, distributed systems, cloud/DevOps, data/AI literacy and capstone.
Learning-day rule
Day 1 means the next planned study session. If a topic needs extra time, repeat/revise it before moving on. Extra sessions do not change the planned sequence.
Comfortable pace
Suggested rhythm: 4–5 learning sessions per week when college allows. Most sessions are 75–120 minutes. Use a 30–45 minute light mode during busy weeks.
Mastery rule
Do not mark a topic complete because you watched a video. Explain it, implement a variation, test edge cases and apply it.
Project rule
Projects evolve through versions in the same repository. A version is unlocked by prerequisite skills, not by a date. Do not start all projects at once.
Language strategy
Java first. Then C for systems foundations, Python for automation/data, JavaScript then TypeScript for frontend. Kotlin/Go/Rust are optional later explorations, not mandatory core tracks.
No guarantee
This roadmap improves preparation; it cannot guarantee a job. Hiring depends on demonstrated skill, interviews, market conditions, communication and applications.
College priority
GTU coursework and exams matter. Pause the learning sequence during exam-heavy periods; resume at the next unfinished learning day.
Use of resources
Resources listed are free official docs, free courses or openly available books/materials. Some platforms have optional paid features; use only free content.
Daily workflow
Recall → learn → trace → practise → debug → project only when ready → write remarks → schedule revision.
Revision
Revision Tracker gives +3, +7, +21 and +45 learning-day checkpoints. Treat these as prompts, not rigid deadlines.
Practice platform
Use self-designed exercises first. Use LeetCode after prerequisites are taught. Never copy solutions before attempting.
Project count
The catalogue includes 25 project ideas at different sizes. You are not expected to build all simultaneously; quality and completion matter more than the count.
Folder convention
Keep practice and projects separate. Use the canonical folders in Project Milestones. Add a README, tests and run instructions before presenting a project.
Status tracking
In Daily Roadmap, set Status to Not started / In progress / Done / Needs revision / Skipped. Add blockers and next steps in Remarks.
Optional Android track
Native Android app-building is a separate side track. Start it when Java/OOP fundamentals are stable and pause it whenever college or Phase 1 needs attention.
Full-detail sequence

This verified edition preserves all 1,029 learning sessions from the original full-detail roadmap: 429 Phase 1 sessions and 600 Phase 2 sessions. Repeated concept, worked-example, guided implementation, independent-practice, edge-case and mastery sessions are intentionally retained.
Pace reality

At 4–5 learning sessions per week, 1,029 sessions take roughly 4–5 years. Treat Sem 3–8 as the main academic planning horizon, not a promise that every advanced session must be finished by Sem 8. Protect GTU study and extend the roadmap when needed.
Project Version Timeline

Use the Project Version Timeline as a planning aid. V1 target days match Project Milestones. Later target days are approximate learning-day anchors; unlock a version only when its prerequisites and acceptance checks are met. Android entries use the separate Android Side Track.
